comment: The phrase “established and openly governed standards” is applied broadly to standards with differing access, licensing, participation, and intellectual-property arrangements. SNOMED CT, for example, has licensing conditions despite recognised governance processes.

anchor.note: p.74 l.Lines 810-819 read as the printed page; section 3.6.2 agrees

public.text: The phrase “established and openly governed standards” is applied broadly to standards with differing access, licensing, participation, and intellectual-property arrangements. SNOMED CT, for example, has licensing conditions despite recognised governance processes.
public.suggestedRevision: Use “recognised standards governed through established standards-development or maintenance processes,” and document relevant licensing, access, localisation, and implementation conditions separately.
